_note: v2 hook overrides for la Pharmacie (B18_pharmacie). Source hooks are kept where the painting shows them; these replace hooks whose painted scene differs. Medical content is kept gentle: no blood; the needle words are a knitting needle and a blank plaque.

fr_drogue_noun.why: Harmful-substance word, so it is shown only as a blank plaque with no writing.
fr_drogue_noun.note: Means harmful or illegal drugs; a medicine from the pharmacy is un médicament.

fr_pharmacie_noun.why: A sea captain holds the telescope in the painting, not a grandma.

fr_pilule_noun.why: The cushion is painted round, not pill-shaped.
fr_pilule_noun.note: 'La pilule' also means the birth-control pill.

fr_pharmacien_noun.why: He carries a tray rather than handing out cough drops, and stands on the right of the shop.

fr_traitement_noun.why: The box marks the bear receiving the treatment, so it stays separate from le pharmacien.

fr_sirop_noun.why: The painting shows two kittens, not three ducklings (the ducklings are in the toy display case).

fr_flacon_noun.why: No paper funnel is painted; the mouse and its vial carry the hook.

fr_remede_noun.why: Painted as a beekeeper (honey), not a grandma, so it does not repeat the knitting granny.

fr_platre_noun.why: The platter is on the floor, not a worktable.

fr_medicament_noun.why: Matches the painting; the floor, not the counter.
fr_medicament_noun.note: For an illegal drug, French uses la drogue instead.

fr_vitamine_noun.why: The ant pushes the ball along the bottom of the display case rather than lifting it.

fr_aiguille_noun.why: Text pass 2026-10-28 (hook lint): respelling (ay-GWEE) -> (ay-GWEEY) to match the card.
